steps.text: Combine sugar and orange juice in a medium saucepan over medium heat; stir until sugar dissolves. Add cranberries and cook, stirring occasionally, until most of the berries have popped and the sauce looks slightly thickened, about 10 minutes.
Transfer to a bowl. The sauce will look loose while hot but will thicken as it cools. Let cool, then serve or cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Sauce with Orange Juice
raw_recipe.description: This easy cranberry sauce with orange juice combines fresh cranberries, sugar, and citrus for a sweet-tart Thanksgiving and holiday side.

video.description: Easy and sweet with just the right tartness, it’s the perfect cranberry sauce for Thanksgiving and Christmas dinners. Try it with your turkey sandwiches, too! This easy, crowd-pleasing recipe is a great addition to your Thanksgiving dinner menu.

review.reviewBody: I needed to try this recipe before serving it to 28 guests this Thanksgiving. 1st, I made this recipe exactly as specified. I did see the words.. "simmer until cranberries pop" and decided to use "frying screen" over the pot. Thank goodness! LOL The recipe is marvelous as it is. Then I made it a 2nd time, using 1 bag cranberries, 1/2 cup brown and 1/2 cup of white sugar, 2/3 cup OJ and 1/4 cup of water. I couldn't justify boiling down Gran Manier, so I added 2 Tablespoons AFTER the berry mixture was done heating. LUCIOUS!!!! Remember to use a spatter screen and let the sauce set for at least 4 hours. Perfect consistancy and texture as well as flavors. YUM!

This was wonderful sauce. I made it especially for my Dad as he loves cranberry sauce with his turkey. Both him and my grandmother raved at how awesome it was. I did make a few changes as suggested by other reviewers: I used half white & half brown sugar, half water & half orange juice. I also put just a touch (probably less than 1/8 tsp) of cinnamon. Thank you so much for sharing such a great recipe - it made a wonderful addition to my family's Thanksgiving dinner!

Excellent recipe! The only thing I altered based on other reviews: 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup white sugar, 1/2 cup orange juice, 1/4 tspn cinnamon n nutmeg with 12oz bag of fresh cranberries. Cooked the sugar n oj together on a med heat for about 6 mins; added the cranberries; allowed them to do their magic for about 10-12 mins with the occasional stir; mashed up towards the end with a potato masher....then added the spices and lowered the temp to a low for another 6 mins. The sauce jelly'd up very, very nicely, the sweetness was at my right level with just a hint of tartness as well as a hint of nutmeg n cinnamon.

I made this recipe by not following your recipe at all. instead, I used 1/3 cup brown sugar, 2/3 cup white sugar, a package of cranberries, and 1.3 cups of freshly squeezed tangerine juice. I added one clove, a little bit of cinnamon, and smoked a doobie of high quality indica as I let it slowly simmer, at medium low for 30 minutes instead of 15 minutes on medium, allowing the reduction to occur slower, thickening the final product even better.

This is a great simple recipe which I go to every year for Thanksgiving. I reduce the sugar and use 1/2 cup brown sugar . I add 1-2 tablespoons of rum or bourbon when boiling and some cinnamon! Sometimes I put in orange zest. Another author in a review wrote that they use some fresh grated ginger which sounds delicious.

I use fresh orange juice! I zest the oranges before I use the juice. I only add 1 teaspoon of zest to the cranberry sauce. I save the rest to use in other recipes. It makes the orange flavor really pop and the kitchen smells amazing! Sometimes I add just a sprinkle of cinnamon as well!

Great recipe! I utilized other reviewers modifications: 1/2 cup brown and 1/2 cup of white sugar, 2/3 cup OJ and 1/4 cup of water; I let the mixture cool 5-10 minutes and used a potato masher to mash up the cranberries. This was delicious and I will definitely make again..

After reading a number of reviews, I used half brown and half white sugar, orange zest, and Contreau after taking it off the heat. Delicious! Note: I cook it in a Dutch Oven as I triple the recipe to give to friends for Christmas. Another advantage of using a Dutch Oven is that it doesn't splatter.

I added a tablespoonful of orange zest to the recipe. If you cook all but 1/4 cup of cranberries as listed, then add them near the end you get a more tart dish. I've cooked both ways and we've enjoyed the cranberries either way. If you rather have less sweetness use water instead of juice and increase the zest. I used lemon zest once, forgot to get oranges, and it was nearly as good. Thank you for this basic recipe.

This is incredibly easy to make, and I have been using this recipe for years. I do make some adjustments though. I use dark brown sugar instead of white and I add about a teaspoon (maybe a little more) of cinnamon and about a quarter teaspoon of nutmeg to it, which make great additions to the cranberries.

My family and I love this cranberry sauce with orange juice. We actually refer to it as cranberry orange relish. If you are bringing some or serving some I would definitely recommend to double the recipe. And if you wanted to bring it to a gathering I’d definitely put it into a 32 oz mason jar with a ribbon for a nice touch. Another secret that makes this even tastier is adding a lot of orange zest after it starts to become jelled and before putting it into the container you choose to use, then add more zest on top. Don’t refrigerate until completely cool. Just my preference.
Yes I substituted Molasses brown sugar instead of white & halved the amount 🤗
Everytime I make this it is a hit with everyone, even some who claim to not like cranberry sauce. Fresh is definitely the way to go.
I have been appointed the cranberry sauce maker for family holidays for the last five years. This recipe is very simple and delicious.

First time making cranberry sauce at home and I used half cup sugar, half cup brown sugar, and squeezed oranges for the juice, added one cinnamon stick, and 1 tablespoon of orange zest. Delicious! So good with stuffing!
Followed the advice on a few reviews, did 1/2 C brown sugar and white sugar, also added 1TBSP orange zest

I used fresh squeezed tangerine juice since that was all I had. Half of my cranberries were strained from a red sangria which added a nice touch. At the end of cooking the cranberries, I added pomegranate arils from the sangria. It’s fantastic.
Added a little lemon juice and a stick of cinnamon while it is cooking. Yummy!
Delicious

This was my first time making cran sauce. It had a little bitter aftertaste. I conservatively sprinkled ground cardamom, stirred, tasted. Just a couple light sprinkles and it took away the bitterness without over taking the sauce.
